subject.title: fix(telegram): surface diagnostic warning when inline keyboard buttons silently dropped due to 64-byte callback_data limit

question: After the false text-only diagnostic is fixed and live proof is supplied, should this land as a diagnostics-only mitigation while the canonical issue remains open for a caller-visible result?
rationale: The canonical report permits a warning as a minimum but describes safety-gated workflows where logs do not inform the calling agent; repository evidence does not establish whether diagnostics alone are the accepted permanent contract.

options.title: Land mitigation, keep issue open
options.body: Merge the accurate diagnostic after live proof and retain https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106996 for structured caller-visible degradation behavior.

options.title: Require caller-visible warning
options.body: Hold this PR until the message-tool result or failure path tells the caller that the keyboard was removed.

options.title: Keep diagnostics only
options.body: Treat operator logs as the complete supported behavior and close the canonical issue after this PR lands.

recommendation.title: Land mitigation, keep issue open
recommendation.body: Merge the accurate diagnostic after live proof and retain https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106996 for structured caller-visible degradation behavior.
